vision.weight_distribution: increased lateral and forefoot/heel loading with reduced midfoot contact
vision.notes: Very high measured arch height (74.2 mm) relative to length with a distally-positioned peak (0.62) and a narrow midfoot on the plantar render suggests pes cavus, which typically pairs with a supinated (underpronated) hindfoot and diminished midfoot contact. Weight distribution here is an estimate inferred from arch morphology, not a measured plantar pressure map; partial/fragmented renders reduce confidence.

vision.weight_distribution: increased lateral heel and forefoot loading with reduced midfoot contact
vision.notes: Arch height of 38mm against a 240mm length yields a high arch index, and the very high width-to-length ratio with limited midfoot contact suggests a cavus, supinatory foot that shifts load to the heel and metatarsal heads. Pressure zones are estimated from arch type and foot geometry, not from a measured plantar pressure map, and mesh artifacts in the renders limit certainty.

vision.notes: Very high arch height (52.3 mm) relative to length and a notably narrow width (40.9 mm) suggest a rigid pes cavus foot with reduced midfoot ground contact, which typically underpronates/supinates and shifts load to heel and metatarsal heads. Pressure zones are estimated from arch morphology and foot geometry, not from a measured pressure map.

reference.title: Captured, reconstructed, measured
reference.note: One foot capture, reconstructed to a watertight millimetre-scale 3D mesh, measured, and read for biomechanics — the whole pipeline end to end.
